name: Basilica
note: c = −1, the middle of the round bulb on the left of the Mandelbrot set. A string of rounded beads, and the figure in Kučera’s paper.

name: San Marco
note: c = −3/4, where the round bulb on the left of the Mandelbrot set touches its heart-shaped body. The Basilica’s beads have run together into one scalloped shell.

name: Douady rabbit
note: The centre of the largest bulb on top of the Mandelbrot set. Three lobes meet at every pinch. The lobes stand out better at about 24 iterations.

name: Airplane
note: Near −1.755 on the x-axis, the middle of the small copy of the Mandelbrot set far out on its left spike. A thin spine strung with spiky beads.

name: Cauliflower
note: c = 1/4, the tip of the dent on the right of the Mandelbrot set’s heart-shaped body. A smooth gourd whose frilled rim is the 2D cauliflower.

name: Siegel disc
note: On the rim of the Mandelbrot set’s heart-shaped body, at an angle set by the golden ratio. A smooth slab with a frilled edge.

name: Dendrite
note: c = i, the tip of a thin hair on top of the Mandelbrot set. The 2D set has no inside, so the solid is a thin branching coral.

name: Kokopelli
note: The middle of a tiny copy of the Mandelbrot set, on a hair above its largest top bulb. A beaded coral.

name: Fat rabbit
note: The point where the largest top bulb joins the Mandelbrot set’s heart-shaped body. The rabbit’s lobes have swollen into one slab with a frilled edge.

name: Feigenbaum point
note: Near −1.4012 on the x-axis, where the row of ever smaller bulbs on the left of the Mandelbrot set ends. A flat, spiny rod.

name: Golden ratio
note: About −0.618 on the x-axis, inside the Mandelbrot set’s heart-shaped body. A smooth lens with a scalloped rim.

name: −0.8 + 0.156i
note: Just outside the Mandelbrot set, in the valley between its heart-shaped body and the round bulb on the left. A row of bulbs about to come apart. They are still fused at 14 iterations: raise the iterations to about 24.

name: 0.285 + 0.01i
note: Just outside the Mandelbrot set, in the dent on its right. In 3D it is almost the Cauliflower’s gourd.

name: −0.4 + 0.6i
note: Just outside the Mandelbrot set’s heart-shaped body, at its upper left. A slab with a frilled edge.

name: −0.70176 − 0.3842i
note: Outside the Mandelbrot set, at the lower left of its heart-shaped body. Clusters of buds on a chain. They are still fused at 14 iterations: raise the iterations to about 24.

name: −0.835 − 0.2321i
note: Outside the Mandelbrot set, just below the round bulb on its left. Curled ribbons. They are still fused at 14 iterations: raise the iterations to about 24.

name: −0.7269 + 0.1889i
note: Barely outside the Mandelbrot set, in the valley between its two largest parts. A scalloped shell, close to the San Marco.

name: 0.45 + 0.1428i
note: Well outside the Mandelbrot set, to its right. The solid breaks into rings of islands.

name: Cracked Basilica
note: The Basilica pushed a little off the x-axis. With one plane it stays a smooth Basilica. The cracks of the name belong to the earlier version: choose Sphere inversions, two planes in the Approach section.

name: Thorn crystal
note: Just off the x-axis, where the round bulb on the left of the Mandelbrot set ends. Flat blades edged with thorns.

name: Split conch
note: The San Marco pushed off the x-axis. With one plane it is a smooth conch. The long crack of the name belongs to the earlier version: choose Sphere inversions, two planes in the Approach section.

name: Flint
note: Inside the Mandelbrot set’s heart-shaped body, a little off the x-axis. With one plane it is a smooth egg with a frilled band. The split stone of the name belongs to the earlier version: choose Sphere inversions, two planes in the Approach section.

name: Plated egg
note: Near the middle of the Mandelbrot set’s heart-shaped body, a little off the x-axis. With one plane it is a smooth egg. The shifted plates of the name belong to the earlier version: choose Sphere inversions, two planes in the Approach section.

name: Plated ball
note: At c = 0 the set is a plain ball, and this is a small step away from it. With one plane it stays a smooth ball. The plates of the name belong to the earlier version: choose Sphere inversions, two planes in the Approach section.

name: Cracked gourd
note: The Cauliflower pushed off the x-axis. With one plane it is a smooth gourd with a few dimples. The cracks of the name belong to the earlier version: choose Sphere inversions, two planes in the Approach section.

name: Pitted gourd
note: In the dent on the right of the Mandelbrot set, a little off the x-axis. A gourd eaten into pits. There are more of them in the earlier version: choose Sphere inversions, two planes in the Approach section.
